subject: soulScythe
pitch:
Category: Fantasy weapon.
Subject: dragonbone soul scythe.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm reviewing the proportions and attachment points, noting the blade reads correctly as a thin edge from the side, but the skull looks too small relative to the scythe's scale.

The wisps feel scattered too far from the base and should pull in closer, while the ribs and claws on the dais already read well. I'm also considering thickening the haft's grip radius for a chunkier, more heroic feel, and checking whether the soul orb needs a visual connection to the rest of the model rather than floating disconnected.

I'm planning to add bone-tendril rods linking the orb to the blade's inner crescent edge, forming a cradle with two connection points to fix that loose-part issue, and double-checking the blade mount joint where it meets the haft.

The skull looks too small compared to the blade, so I'm thinking about whether to scale the whole head proportionally. Scaling the positional offsets through the H function wouldn't help since the hardcoded geometry sizes themselves wouldn't grow, so I'll need another approach to make the skull more prominent.

I'll add a bone crest/frill behind the skull—swept-back spiked fins extruded along a plane, bridging the head to the blade and filling out the silhouette, working out the extrusion thickness direction and placement along the side of the skull.

Checking the frill edges confirm no self-intersection, so I'll place it at the head joint with a bone-colored tint, skipping the extra membrane glow inset for simplicity. Now I'm thinking about repositioning the wisps closer to the head.

The wisps are a bit far from the base but still read fine, so I'll leave them. I'm also thickening the haft and bumping up the band radii so they don't get clipped by the thicker shaft.

Now I'm adding the orb cradle struts, sweeping catmull curves between points near the orb to create support structures.

Still refining the strut geometry and checking uniqueness of each sweep/band signature before adding the frill loop insertion point.
